entities.summary:
Johann Heß (1500-1547) was a German Lutheran theologian and Protestant Reformer of Breslau. Born in the Holy Roman Empire, Heß studied at the University of Leipzig and later became a prominent figure in the Lutheran movement.

 Heß's most significant contribution to the Protestant Reformation was his translation of the Bible into German, which made scripture more accessible to ordinary people. His work also emphasized the importance of personal faith and spiritual discipline, influencing many subsequent Lutheran theologians.

 As a key figure associated with the Breslau movement, Heß played a crucial role in shaping the theological landscape of 16th-century Germany. His legacy continues to be felt today, particularly in the realm of Lutheran theology and biblical studies.

 In his own words, 'The Word of God is not just a book, but a living, breathing presence that guides us on our spiritual journey.' - Johann Heß
